children.label: Original source instructions
children.help_text:
Instructions:  On this form, you will attach the R&R Subaward Budget (Fed/Non-Fed) files for your grant application.  Complete the subawardee budget(s) in  accordance with the R&R (Fed/Non-Fed) budget instructions.  Please remember that any files you attach must be a PDF document.

Important: Please attach your subawardee budget file(s) with the file name of the subawardee organization.  Each file name must be unique. 

Original template-extraction instruction: Click here to extract the R&R Budget (Fed/Non-Fed) Attachment

The Adobe PDF version of the R&R Budget (Fed/Non-Fed) 5 Year Form will be compressed and embedded into this form.  The applicant will click the button and a dialog box will appear where applicant indicates where to save the file.

The extraction button belongs to the original PDF workflow. This preview displays the instruction and accepts illustrative file references; it does not extract a template, upload a file or submit a budget.

children.post_populated: The source imports the completed budget form beneath BudgetAttachments. Application integration must extract/resolve and validate each completed original budget PDF against this exact source form; it is not another applicant data-entry question.

notes: The original DAT and XSD make all source attachment slots optional (0–10). Agency/program requirements remain additional instructions; do not impose an invented minimum of one file.

Finite XML slot bindings preserve each ATT1–ATT10 source coordinate. The capture list is ordered and compact; actual service assignment to numbered source slots remains integration work, not arbitrary sparse-slot round-trip proof.

Source ATTn elements are xs:string file references. The current library Attachment scalar is a UUID service reference. This is an explicit capture projection, not a serializer that writes UUIDs as source file descriptors.

BudgetAttachments contains full imported completed-budget XML. The explicit External form source reference preserves that separate derived-payload channel; the child budget is not modeled as inline applicant questions, compiled or qualified by this definition.

Template extraction, actual PDF format/content, original-template preservation, filename conventions/uniqueness, file existence/ownership and source XML construction require real application/attachment integration. No upload or XML mapping is implemented here.
No equivalent implementation was found by the pinned SGG inventory at48d93f882c63a711bdec4b16e3150d1293cdff43. Existing-SGG behavior/runtime parity is not claimed.
Original source instructions, extraction wording and important warning are preserved in displayed plan/layout prose. The template-extraction control is not represented as a fake working button.
risks: Synthetic UUIDs are sample references with no uploaded file behind them. Schema admission does not establish file content, filename uniqueness, template correctness, upload ownership, parsed external budget validity or a successful application submission.

The source external budget reference is an explicit not-compared/integration boundary. Passing the applicant-capture/source-reference checks must not be reported as successful child budget or source XML generation.

Original DAT FILE row 1-0 declares a maximum of 30 and reports an invalid attachment filename; it does not explicitly settle the unit or conflict with unrestricted XSD ATT strings and the imported generic FileName 1–255 facet. This exact source difference is recorded. The UUID reference is not constrained to 30 characters; actual filename/upload policy requires resolution during integration, not inferred approval from capture schema admission.
